# Scavio

> Scavio is a real-time search API for AI agents. It gives LLMs and autonomous
> agents structured JSON access to 50+ platforms -- search, social, retail, real
> estate, travel, local, jobs, app stores, software reviews, ad libraries and
> company filings -- plus Extract, which reads any URL as Markdown, plain text
> or raw HTML. One REST API, one key: no HTML parsing, no browser automation,
> no proxy management. A cost-effective alternative to Tavily, SerpAPI, and
> Apify with broader platform coverage.

Homepage: https://scavio.dev
Docs: https://scavio.dev/docs
Pricing: https://scavio.dev/pricing
Dashboard / free API key (50 signup credits, no card): https://dashboard.scavio.dev

## What Scavio Does

Scavio returns machine-readable JSON built for LLM tool calling and agentic
workflows. Every data endpoint is a POST, and every platform below is live in
production today.

Credits: most endpoints cost 1 credit. Four surfaces are priced by the request
body rather than a flat per-route number -- Walmart (by `domain`), Threads (by
identifier), Kuaishou (per endpoint) and Extract (by `mode`) -- so a single
"costs N credits" is wrong for those. Per-platform pricing is stated inline
below.

## API Endpoints

Scavio serves 780 endpoints across 109 platforms, Extract included (100 platform families in the API, since Google's verticals share one).
Every data endpoint is a POST returning structured JSON (crawl and batch job status is a GET, cancel a DELETE; the Google Custom Search compatible endpoint is a GET). Most cost 1 credit;
the exceptions are stated per platform below.

#### Publix (1 credit, every endpoint; publix.com (US: FL, GA, AL, SC, NC, TN, VA, KY), English; every price endpoint takes store_id (a Publix store number, stores[].store_id; 9999 is the site's placeholder = 400; an unknown store = charged 404) and echoes store { id, name }; THE KEY FACT: publix.com shows prices only for items on sale (weekly ad, BOGO, multi-buys, Extra Savings) and for order-ahead (In-Store Pickup) deli and bakery items, so price is null for everything else, never estimated (no regular shelf prices; delivery and curbside run through Instacart at prices Publix says are higher than in store); search (query) and category (category_url /c/<name>/<id> or category_id GUID) share one grid: 48 items/page, pages up to 100, total and total_pages, sorts relevance (default), featured, name_asc, name_desc, popularity, savings_amount, most_viewed, filters on_sale, bogo, brand, facets with counts; each item has item_code (Publix item code, not a UPC: Publix publishes no UPCs), base_product_id, title, brand, size, description, image, url, category_path, aisle (at that store, e.g. "Aisle 11 - Lunch Meat"), on_sale, price, price_unit (lb), bundle {quantity, price} (multi-buys, price null), starting_price ("Starts at" items), regular_price, price_text and regular_price_text as shown, promo {type single / bogo / multi, message, conditions, savings, valid_from, valid_through}, has_coupon, is_order_ahead; keywords the site sends to an order-ahead page set redirected_to (items may be empty); no match = empty 200; product by item_code: the card plus nutrition labels (one per component and size for deli subs) and, for order-ahead items, short_description, lead_time, serves, calories (no ingredients, allergens, UPC or reviews; Publix does not publish them online); categories = 16 departments, 382 nodes (id, name, url, parent_id, level, children; parent_id = a subtree; store_id optional); weekly-ad = the store's current English ad, about 700 items (store 1614 Miami: 691 incl. 229 BOGO and 20 B2G1, 2026-11-12 to 11-18), ad {start_date, end_date}, departments, filters department, bogo_only (BOGO and B2G1), query; items id, item_code, title, description, brand, department, categories, savings_text as shown, deal_type (bogo, b2g1, multi, price, percent_off, other), price (plain price only), price_unit, bundle, save_up_to, additional_savings, min_quantity, fine_print, stacked_with_coupon, promotion, valid_from, valid_to, image; ads run Thursday-Wednesday in Florida and Wednesday-Tuesday in Georgia and North Carolina (stores[].weekly_ad_break_day per store); some ad prices differ by store (24-pack Michelob Ultra $25.99 Miami, $28.49 Atlanta, $23.49 Charlotte on 2026-11-13); extra-savings = several hundred temporary price reductions (678 to 1,363 per store) with savings_text, savings, final_price as the site lists it, min_quantity, size, url and period {start_date, end_date}; coupons = the store's digital coupons (about 100-130) with value, min_quantity, limit_per_transaction, categories, valid dates, terms, read-only (never clipped, no account); savings-search = one query across the weekly ad, Extra Savings and coupons, items tagged saving_type weekly_ad / extra_savings / coupon; order-ahead = the deli and bakery order-ahead menu with the store's prices, section subs (default, Pub Subs) or all (about 1,150 items), 60/page up to 50 pages, plus lead_time, serves, calories, pay_online (Chicken Tender Sub $12.09 Miami, $11.99 Atlanta and Charlotte on 2026-11-13); stores by zip, city + state or store_id, limit up to 30, radius_miles up to 100: store_id, name, type, address, phone, 7 days of hours, departments, services, pharmacy {phone, hours}, liquor_store, coordinates, distance_miles, weekly_ad_break_day, opening_date; suggestions = up to 10 search-box suggestions and, with store_id, up to 4 products; no ratings or reviews, UPCs, ingredients, allergens, coupon clipping, Club Publix account data, cart, ordering, pharmacy data beyond phone and hours, Spanish ad or price history; failed upstream calls are not charged, a not-found (unknown store, item code or category) is a charged 404)

deals (tr): type flash (slots {tag, status active / upcoming, date, start, end} and the active slot's items, or slot = a dated tag from slots[].tag) or super_discounts (campaign items at a 10 / 14 / 30-day low and at least 30% off); coupons (tr; content_id, seller_id = another seller's listing, default the buy box): coupons {id, discount, discount_type amount / percent, max_discount, min_basket, currency, valid_until, issued_by, seller_id, link, mega_coupon, plus_members_only, messages}; coupons belong to each seller (the buy box often has none); rankings (category_id required; best_seller default, most_favourited, most_rated, top_viewed; 20 per page, 5 pages = the top 100): rank, content_id, name, brand, prices, lowest_price_badge, badges, rating, review_count, in_stock, seller; suggestions (query): text, type keyword / category / brand / store, url, category_ids, brand_id, seller_id, image; delivery (content_id, optional item_number, listing_id; city_id and district_id on tr only, e.g. Istanbul 133, Sisli 54; no city list): every seller listing's delivery {start, end}, ships_by, ships_in_days, tomorrow / same-day shipping cutoffs, rush_delivery_hours, local_delivery, seller, buy_box, time_zone; no price history, numeric 30-day lowest price, pickup points, cart, checkout, Plus or Trendyol GO data; calls usually take 1-15 s, flash deals up to about a minute (client timeout 120 s); Trendyol's Partner API is for marketplace sellers and their integrators with seller-panel credentials, with no public catalog, price or review API; failed upstream calls are not charged, a not-found (product, category, brand, seller, list) is a charged 404)

product on 38 (not mo, tw or the shared EU store countries: use search or stock there); stores on 46 (not mo); ae, eg, id, th, br, cn (separate H&M sites), al, az, ba, by, cl, co, cr, ge, is, kh, kz, mk, nz, pe, xk, za (no online store), ru and uk (use gb) answer 400 (unbilled); search (query; department women / men / kids / baby / home; store = a store code: that store's assortment), category (category = H&M's category id such as ladies_dresses or men_jeans, the same in every market; returns everything filed under the id), deals (department, default women; the sale grid, empty between sales: 25 of 47 markets had an empty women's sale grid on 2026-11-15) and new-arrivals (department, default women) share one grid: page up to 200, page_size 1-72 (default 36), sorts relevance, newest, price_asc, price_desc, filters color, size, material, fit, product_type (facet values of an earlier answer in the same market, up to 10, ORed) and on_sale (not on deals); grid fields items, count, total, page, page_size, total_pages, sort, sorts_offered, filters, facets, on_sale_count, price_range; items have article_code, product_code, title, brand, url, prices, currency, promo_text, multipack, color, colors, sizes {size_code, label, in_stock}, in_stock, coming_soon, new_arrival, markers (e.g. ARKET, Weekday on items H&M sells), category, image; product (article_code or url): category, breadcrumbs, description, composition, materials, care, attributes (fit, length, rise, sleeve_length, style, neckline, weight), prices, colors with their own prices, sizes {in_stock, few_left}, images, rating {average, count} and the latest reviews H&M shows (up to 10: rating, text, date, fit feedback; no names); no full review list; usually 4-60 s; stock (article_code or product_code): colors {article_code, name, sizes {size_code, label, in_stock, few_left}}, sizes_total, sizes_in_stock; online stock, not store stock (H&M publishes no per-size store stock); few_left null on mo, tw and the shared EU store; stores (city, postal_code, or lat / lng with radius_km default 25; page_size 1-100, default 20): store_code, name, status, store_class, address, city, state, postal_code, lat, lng, phone, opening_hours, opening_hour_exceptions, departments, campaigns, distance_km, total, country_total (478 US stores); suggestions (query): suggestions {text, type query or content, url}; production (article_code or url): production_countries, countries {country, suppliers {supplier_id, name, factories {factory_id, name, city, workers}}}, no street addresses; no price history (poll and store your own), per-size store stock, full review list, member-only cart prices, or the COS, Weekday, & Other Stories, Monki and ARKET stores; H&M has no public product, price or stock API (H&M Group's integration portals are for business partners, behind a sign-in); calls usually take 1-10 s, product 4-60 s (client timeout 120 s); failed upstream calls are not charged, a not-found is a charged 404)
